'This is true love, I will go call Mom!' The meaning hinges on 'this' working together with 'will call' in spoken Russian.

'Well, that is of course far from everything.' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'everything' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Eva answers right away.

'Kostya, what are you lost in thought about now?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Kostya' before landing on 'become lost in thought'.
Знаешь, я тут серьёзно думаю.
'You know, I am thinking seriously here.' Kostya brings out the contrast between 'know' and 'I' in a few short words.
Интересно, кто на самом деле сильней?
'I wonder who is actually stronger?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'interesting' and finishing on 'stronger'.
Большая белая акула или злой крокодил?
'A great white shark or an angry crocodile?' Kostya anchors the line on 'big', while 'crocodile' completes the thought.
Может, лучше обсудим это в постели?
'Maybe we should discuss this in bed instead?' The grammar packs 'maybe' and 'bed' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Отличная идея, чур, я буду акулой!
'Great idea, dibs on being the shark!' Notice how Russian expresses 'great' and 'shark' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Не мог же я такое рассказать!
'I could not possibly tell that story!' The meaning hinges on 'not' working together with 'to tell' in spoken Russian.
Тем более прямо при моей Насте.
'Especially right in front of my Nastya.' Notice how Russian expresses 'that' and 'proper name' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Мама тоже очень рада за нас.
'Mom is also very happy for us.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'mom' before landing on 'us'. Kostya answers right away.
Я же всегда говорю только правду.
